newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to launch power cuts to save electricity.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to launch power cuts to save electricity.

text.p: A dry spell affecting Ecuador's main hydroelectric dam will force the country to launch power cuts to ration electricity, officials at a government agency said Monday.

"The water flow in Central Paute (dam) has fallen dramatically to 35 cubic meters per second and therefore, starting Wednesday, we will ration 20 percent of electric power," said Donald Castillo, president of Ecuador's Inecel energy institute.
He said the cuts would be made in rotating shifts of four to five hours.
Only three of the 10 turbines of Central Paute, which supplies 70 percent of the country's electricity, were working because of the drought.
Paute is located some 440 km (270 miles) south of Quito.
Castillo warned rationing would continue until measures to solve the energy shortage were taken, such as the signing of new contracts with private utility companies.
Last year Ecuador faced its worst energy crisis in 15 years, and Incel estimates annual investments of $250 million are needed to avoid future problems.
In the last five months of 1995, power cuts lasting up to eight hours daily caused industrial production losses of $500 million, according to official estimates.
But no relief was in sight.
"We think the rains likely over the high areas of the Paute basin will only be a drizzle, which will not solve the problem," said Antonio Rodriguez of the National Water and Weather Institute.
